corrected_draft.description_long: Reuters reported on February 7, 2025, that DOGE staff had begun work at the Department of Energy. A subsequent Senate letter asked the department whether staff had accessed sensitive nuclear-security information. The article and letter document concerns and a request for clarification; neither establishes access to NNSA personnel files. The Post reported that the commercial mortgage unit did not do business with Trump again, while later private-banking loans for the Washington hotel and Doral were separate transactions handled by another division. corrected_draft.title: Trump discusses DeJoy and postal funding at press briefing
corrected_draft.description_short: At an August 15, 2020 press briefing, President Trump said he did not know what Postmaster General Louis DeJoy was doing and opposed postal funding tied to mail-in voting.
corrected_draft.description_medium: Trump’s remarks linked the funding debate to mail ballots, but he did not say he had directed DeJoy to remove sorting machines or slow delivery. DeJoy’s operational changes were separately reported and contested; a direct order from Trump is not established here. He argued that ballots would be subject to loss or delay, while saying he did not know what DeJoy was doing.
corrected_draft.description_long: At a White House press briefing on August 15, 2020, President Trump discussed reports that postal ballots might not arrive before Election Day and argued that Congress had not approved funding he said was needed for universal mail voting and Postal Service operations. He distinguished absentee ballots requested by voters from universal mail-in voting and criticized the latter. When a reporter asked whether he supported DeJoy’s recent actions, Trump praised the postmaster general but said, “I don’t know what he’s doing.” Trump also said DeJoy would need funding if millions of ballots were processed. The transcript records Trump’s public remarks about funding, mail voting, and DeJoy. It does not record Trump directing DeJoy to remove sorting machines or reduce delivery service.
